rebuttal_or_critique: I remain unconvinced by the majority's insistence on maintaining a 'withdrawal of accommodation' stance. With headline CPI at 3.54% and core inflation at 3.15%, the real policy rate is now clearly in restrictive territory. Using monetary policy to combat food inflation of 5.42%—which is largely a supply-side phenomenon—is a misapplication of our tools that risks unnecessary damage to the growth momentum of 6.80%. The positive output gap of 0.30% is too narrow to justify such a tight stance. I am willing to compromise on the rate cut to achieve a shift in stance to 'neutral', as the current stance is increasingly inconsistent with the inflation trajectory and risks overtightening.
